if you like J-RPG's then this is a must buy. i have not put much time into it yet but i know, like with many of the other Tales of games, before im done, i will have more then 100 hours in.
now then, what makes this good?
for one, this is a really solid PC port. you can alter the resolution, alter the grapics a little by changing things like draw distance and some other stuff(didn't really look at them too long). you can play with a contoller(360 and even PS3 if you have motion joy) and customise the buttons.
the game its self is quite different from the other Tales of games, for one, there is no transition screen when you enter battles; once you touch an enemy, the battle will start(after the characters move into place and the extra mobs spawn in), and the combat system is similar to Tales of Graces in your basic attacks(known as Martial artes in game) work like a combo system; holding a direction while pressing the button will do a different attack depending on what direction you are holding(but you have to unlock them), and instead of the combo points that Graces and Xilla had, you have a meter that is similar but if it runs out, you will be unable to attack for a short time. it fills up if you idle or block attacks.
the story... well, not very far in but it seems like its nothing really special, but when it comes to Tales of games, its the characters that make it great, and i have seen a few of the party members so far and i find them enjoyable.
the world itself is quite nice looking as well. on top of battles not having loading transitions, several cutscenes dont have pesky transions between them, so you can get into action quite swiftly.
the Voice acting is good in my opinion, some of the VA's are people i have heard before and i enjoyed them. some people may be quick to say they suck, but i have heard terrible VA before(ever play Samurai Legend Musashi on the PS2 before? and who doesn't remember Resident Evil on the Playstation?), so to me, this is good.
Overall, if you are a fan of the Tales of games or J-RPG's in general, this is a must buy. the story is not going to be mind blowing but the gameplay is where the game shines bightest. the Tales of games never really had great storys to them, but with each new Tales of title, they take the battle systems and tweek them to make each game feel different, and try to have a good cast of characters to make the game stand out from the other games.

This review is for those of you who are either already a "Tales of" fan or a jrpg fan
For Jrpg fans:
The "Tales of" series is comprised of isolated mothership titles like Final Fantasy and Dragon Quest (eg. Final Fantasy VII has nothing to do with Final Fantasy XIII but XIII-2 is related to XIII) so you can easily get into this game without playing previous entries. The "Tales of" series isn't well known for their stories in fact I find them all to be pretty weak but one of the strong points is the characters in each story and how they interact with on another, what they do on their adventure, and their overall chemistry is entertaining. The anime cliches can be a turn off for some and unbearable for others but if you can look past that the "Tales of" series offers fun gameplay and is the major reason I became a fan. All the games aren't your traditional turn based rpg game but rather real time "fighter" in which you control a character and attack doing normal attacks and specials to create combos.
This time around in Tales of Zestiria you find yourself fighting on a 3d plane similar to recent entries in the series however to cut down on load times instead of encountering a monster and getting put onto a battle area you instead fight on the overworld map itself fighting from wide open planes to narrow corridors with obstacles here and there every now and then. Overall I think Tales of Zestiria is an ok entry into the series and is a nice little title to get a taste of what "Tales of" has to offer but there are older titles I would highly recommend in its place.
For "Tales of" fans:
Its not PS3 Vesperia or DC Destiny

This game is incredibly short, but I'd rather have a tiny game I really enjoy than a longer game that I'm not having as much fun with. I completed the game twice, back-to-back, and 100%'d it with all achievements each time. When you know what you're doing, you can go for speed runs as the game gives you clear time when you finish.
If you're not a speed run fan, then not to worry: the game doesn't display a clear time until you finish, and it's quite relaxing. The game is visually rather simple and peaceful-looking, with a soft electronic soundtrack that was very enjoyable.
The jist of the game is you touch cement-looking platforms on water, they get brown on the sides with grass on top, and you hop on buttons to trigger more platforms to raise up out of the water until you've raised all of them. Bonus objectives for achievements include collecting several easily found floating cubes, and making every platform grassy, both of which I found to be very easy if you are anal about it from start to finish, and know that if you jump near the top of the rise on a yellow elevator platform, you can go a bit higher to get one tough-to-acquire cube.
This game is very relaxing, from its visuals to its gameplay, to its soundtrack which I really enjoyed. If you want a challenge, then there is virtually none here, save for competing for good speed run times. I was shooting for 100% completion on my second run, and finished in just over 13 minutes...and I'm pretty terrible at going quickly, too! I definitely recommend this game, at least on a sale if you want cheap, short fun.

The graphics are great, the animations smooth, the audio is good as well. But there are several things that make this game simply unenjoyable. Some of them are core design decisions, so not likely to ever change.
1) The mechanic of constantly freezing to death, and having to run from one firepit to another firepit to prevent dying is TERRIBLE for a ranged or mage class. This essentially forces you to either backtrack a ton (which is boring, repetative, and frustrating) or run head long into big groups of enemies. For a melee class, fine, but for ranged or magic class, this is obviously a major problm. This constant death meter at the bottom of the health bar also discourages exploration, discourages testing different playstyles, only creates frustration and boredom.
2) You cannot change difficulty. EVER. Often gamers have no idea how hard a game will be, and like to start out on hard, and maybe turn it down, or start out on normal and crank it up after realizing it's too easy. Sorry. You cannot change the difficulty at any time, whatsoever. The only thing you can do is wipe your entire character and start all over from scratch. How this made it out of alpha and into beta and then into a fully released game is simply astounding.
3) This game seems to me, at least at first, to be very heavily leaned toward a melee character. I chose a ranged bow character, and this did not work out well. After two full levels, and two entire game areas, I still have essentially zero ranged powers. The only power I have is a melee kick. For a ranged char. What? The only thing I can currently do is kick, and shoot a single arrow. Why a ranged character even has a "kick" ability to begin with and nothing else is very confusing. This is why I think the game basically really really really wants you to play as a melee fighter.

OK.  I read alot of reviews about this game, most were negative.  Despite all the complaints, some of which I found were legitimate I bought it anyways because I was desparate for a new hack n slash.  First and foremost you need to know that I got the game on sale for $19.99.  Bottom line for me was that for this price the game was worth buying.  Paying more than $25 for this game would be a hard sell unless you are not on a budget.
So why did I give it a thumbs up?  Most people agreee that the graphics are pretty good and that is true.  I feel that the combat is decent enough to make it interesting.  I love it when enemies  block with shields or become temporarily invincible with an aura surrounding them, as this makes it harder to just spam attacks.  Also the balance of the game is pretty good as enemies don't all die with 1 hit, but also are not damage sponges.
The boses in general are a high point as they are varied and interesting.  Ocassionally I ran into one that was either really easy or really hard, but overall they were fun.
Loot drops.  That is a fundamental weakness in this game.  Rather than looking excitedly at the loot I got at the end of the level, I found myself hoping to get the items I needed to upgrade my Armorer and Blacksmith so they would sell better equipment.   For me it wasn't a game breaker as the equipment you could buy at the vendors were dedent for your level (unless you way overleveled), and you actually craft the items when you buy them and get random enchantments on items that range from magic to unique to legendary.
Legendary Items.  Another disappointment.  While I got a number of legendary items throughout the game, they were generally underwhelming.  I even found myself choosing magic or unique items over legendary ones unless the legendary had the specific enchantments I wanted.  They just weren't that much better than magic or unique loot.
You will want to grind some to get the resources needed to upgrade vendors and blood to level up.  And if you need specific resources for upgrade once you have a merchant you can buy them with gold or trade them for other resources.  I heard a complaint that to buy resources, like if your wanted to buy 500 wood, you would have to click the mouse 500 times.  Well good news!  That is no longer true.  Just hold down and in a few seconds you will have all you need or can afford.
End Game.  I just started a new game plus and all the equipment available and the drops do scale so you get decent items right away.  I also read that you lose all your gear and bonuses when starting a new game plus and keep only your skills.  Well good news!  This has also been fixed.  You keep EVERYTHING from your last game and whatever bonuses you got while leveling up.
In its current state this game really is not bad if you get it on sale.  Its end game is not very strong, so if you are expecting Diable 3 or Grim Dawn you will be disappointed.  If you are expecting a slightly above average, decent length, hack n slash for casual play I think it is definitely better than most people credit it for.
I understand people complaints, and if you are looking to sink 50-100's of hours into a game, this is not it.   But if you are simply looking to scratch your hack n slash itch with something new for 12-20 hours on one playthrough, then you might want to give it a try.   I am sure if I had paid $40 for the game or had gotten caught up in pre-order hype I would not be giving as positive of a review, but going in with low expectations and paying half-price I was pleasantly surprised.

When I first got a chance to play this game on a PlayStation 4 I was jealous of all those PS4 owners out there because I knew that I was missing out on something special, as I don't own a PS4. The thing is that Bloober Team made, in my opinion, a fantastic decision to bring the game to PC, and so I got to really dive into the game.
In a game where it feels like Bomberman hired the cast of Twisted Metal to play a game of lets blow each other up, you will find the game BRAWL. The thing about this game is that it not only gives you solid gameplay, but something that many of us gamers who have spent quite sometime playing video games as we grew up and that is hot seat play. For those who don't know what this is, it's the ability to play with multiple people on one screen/system.
The way that they can do this is that they have an almost top down view of the "arenas" so there's no need for split screen, but there's definitely the need to pay attention, and to make sure that you come out on top. In this game you will be trying to collect power ups to make you a more deadly opponent. There are bomb power ups that allow you to place more bombs, there are strength power ups which allow your bombs to cause more damage, and there's also the very coveted health power up that will allow you 1 extra hit before going down.
There's also a roster of characters that all have their unique talents to help you outwit your opponent. There's an invisibility skill, there's a stun skill, a trap skill, and more. This is a game that you're definitely going to want to play through the story mode for each character. The story modes play out like in-depth tutorials for each character, you will get to learn a little bit of their back story, but at the same time you're going to learn EXACTLY what their skills do, instead of being forced to simply try trial and error.
This game has local matches, online matches, and also has a couple of different game modes to give you a bit of variety. To me this is a very well polished game with a ton of replay value, and there's a good amount of content to experience to maybe even have tournaments to see who the best is at deathmatches or any of the many other modes.
I don't want to say I was surprised with the seamless transition from the PlayStation 4 to the PC, but I was impressed to see that the game looked as good, ran extremely smooth, and felt like it belonged on the PC. Sure you're going to want to get a couple of controllers so that you can play your friends, and I know that there are those out there who will refuse to get a controller for the PC, but this is a game that must be played with a controller if you are going to kick serious♥♥♥♥♥ and I think that if you are a fan of competitive games, bombs, horror themes, and more, you've got to add this game to your collection. This game gets a 9.3 out of 10.

It's a decent game and right now it's worth it on sale, but for the full price as an early access game with very limited gameplay in my honest opinion is not worth the money ( right now in it's current state anyway )
Before i delve deeper into what i think about the game, here are some things i would have liked to know before buying this game, considering i based my purchase on the positive reviews i found here.
- It's a small game, the scale of the game is not as big as you would think for a sandbox survival.
- It's based around avoid wolves alone, until you can get yourself a gun and ammo.
- You will eventually die, you will run out of stuff in this finite world, so the whole premise of the game is to find out how long you can make it, instead of being able to settle down, fish, farm, make ammo and create everything you need to become self susstained. Unfortunatly it's not like that.
+ It's a very small download and runs good ( download was around 950mb at the time of this review )
+ Decent art style even though the world could be a lot more immersive.
+ Good sound
+ Great potential
It's just not riveting enough for me personaly, there is not enough to make you feel like you're in a living breathing portion of the world and it all feels very restrictive which i wouldve loved to have known prior to my purchase, it's fun to avoid the wolves, collect supplies and make the right moves related to the weather outside this i will admit but it's all too very small for my liking and a game like this has to have scale. Most of the positive reviews sold me on this game, but i feel it's all slightly biased based on the fact that this game DOES have huge potential that we are all hoping for, but it's not there right now, it's missing, theres no point in rating something so high whilst being mediocre with the promise of being something special. It's early acess, but you're charging money which does unfortunatly expose you to sharp criticism such as mine.
I've given my money to the developer, hopefully this game gets more content in the future like promised becasuse there is a lot missing right now, this game needs more stuff, more scale, and more of a living world to really become an immersive peice of art. They are on the right track, but i can only give this a thumbs down since i cant vote sideways, i must apologize.
If you're reading this, my rating may change in the future as the game gets updated.

I was raised in Alaska so, not at all ignoring my own subjectivity, I'm just going to say that this is one of the best survival-genre titles out there. Even from the early access days of The Long Dark, I could tell, based on the awesome attention to detail in the quasi cell shaded yet realistic portrayal of bit-like pixels, that this game was in a league all its own.
Erie, quiet, and insightful; these quotes are the first and last bit of civilization you'll encounter that isn't a frozen corpse for the entire game. Your life will consist of three essential goals at all times:
Stay rested, warm, and fed.
Your chief adversary, like in the real wilderness of the Great North, is Old Man Winter himself. A tireless and incremental devil who will constantly whittle away at your desire to continue forth; lulling you into a cold yet eerily peaceful death.
Crafting, hunting, trap laying, and scavenging. It's all here. The game consists of a number of "levels" that are teeming with wildlife both apex and otherwise that will keep your head on a swivel as you search for firewood you can gather or breakdown from chairs, boxes, and the like. If there's an idea you've had for a harsh winter survival title, The Long Dark has likely done it. You need to play The Long Dark just to see how immersive and harrowing it is to believe for yourself.
So huddle close inside the abandoned car you found alongside the desolate highway of a frozen lake as the wolves circle nearby. Let the The Long Dark take you to the edge of Humanity before the inevitability of death wraps its cold fingers around you.

Bomberman is most likely the best multiplayer arena battle game of all time, well in my opinion.  So here we have a modern clone with some twists on the idea.  Main differences are that each character has two special abilities.  One that is reusable on a timer, and one that has limited uses but can be replenished by picking up collectables.  I'm a purist when it comes to pvp, so the idea didn't sound appealling but testing it out in 1 vs 1 local, it was good fun.  It added an extra element to think about.
This is probably needed, as the classic game, which would be my personal preference doesn't have so many bonus's to collect as Bomberman did.  You simply get the basics.  Whereas in Bomberman each player would have the opportunity to get every power up, they are just built into the characters in BRAWL.  So it's different, is it better?  I don't think so.  It's still fun though.
I only played in 1 vs 1, as with all arena games, more players would undoubtably increased the fun a lot more!  I've read a review on here saying the multiplayer online doesn't work.  I haven't been able to try it out yet, the playerbase seems very small and my efforts to find other players has been fruitless so far.
I encountered no bugs or glitches, the game seems solid.  Graphics and sound are good.  It's a nice, fun alternative to the classic Bomberman.  Hopefully the community will grow a bit with time, the games only been released for two weeks.  In the mean time you will need local buddies to play against, unless you're happy to kill bots and do the single player campaign.
Very fun!

This is a quality game. If I could either have 1 really good game, or 10 mediocre games, I would pick Tales of Zestiria.
Look at my Steam Library. See how many hours I have in this game compared to some of my other games. Look at the games I don't really like to play.

And the thing is this is one of the
Tales of Titles.

Overall... I highly recommend this for anyone who is looking to create something like an RPG, and wants to have a system that does just that, instead of many other programs. While the price tag seems a bit hefty, it's a game that's superbly worth the purchase (and compared to many other programs, it's actually light on the price). It may appear a tad daunting to work with at first, it's open freedom becomes a grace rather than something far too open and confusing. In addition, those who aren't savvy with sprite or script creation can either utilize countless online resources to enhance the structure of your game. And if you are a purist, there's still a lot to go for. The program allows for lots of variation and freedom with choices and events, and if it's not included in the base, there's likely an additional script that's been made to do it!
On the DLC:
DLC is a bit hefty, yet it's completely optional. I don't have any of the DLC packs, but I know people that do (so I can offer some words about it). It offers new textures and tools to work with, but you aren't missing too much. If you want something that's offering a different flavor of tools, and you want something "official", it's worth it.
Positives:
+Lots of freedom with the system. Events are very diverse in scale, and pretty much everything can be changed.
+Integration with Steam Community and ability to manually add pre-Steam scripts and projects into your files.
+Base game offers good amount of content to work with, built in tools are good.
+DLC is not a practical requirement.
+Most of the base systems and tools allow for lots of creativity.
Negatives:
-Price tag, but the game goes on sale often. (Still better than many other programs that typically can cost even more)
-Certain aspects are a tad complicated and sometimes a tad confusing for newer users, but it's something that takes time. I recommend looking up reviews online to get a better grasp of the program (the whole easy for a child is a little bit of a stretch)
-Most of the base systems, but not all of them. For all of these to have real depth (IE: The base character creation system, battle) extra resources and online tools are practically necessary for a good looking final product. While I can't give any great recommendations, there's a lot of places to go for these.
-Base resources sometimes leave something to be desired. As with many of the RPG Maker games, the base game goes with a medieval fantasy sort of vibe, so those wanting to make modern style RPGs and the like will need to use resources or DLC.
Overall, despite the negatives, the massive freedom of the system makes this much better than the older titles and what I feel to be the strongest and easily the best RPG Maker I've ever used in the series.

A very difficult and unforgiving indie game by Polish studio Bloober Team. It's basically a modern variation of Bomberman/Dyna Blaster, but way more atmospheric and complex. Your task on each level is usually to kill mobs and bosses using bombs and skills, but there are some tasks and puzzles that have to be completed in a different way. The rooms that you are trapped in are usually quite big and full of traps, like spikes, crates falling on your head or fire, which makes them more interesting and difficult to beat.
You can play as one of several characters - each of them has its own, individual set of abilities that alter the gameplay. Clown, for example, can sneeze to push bombs onto his enemies or create decoys, and the little girl with a teddy bear on her head is able to throw a knife and teleport to its location, switching places with enemies that got stabbed. If you wish to survive and complete more than two levels of story mode, or stand a chance in multiplayer, you really need to learn using those abilities to your advantage. Fortunately, the game includes a separate tutorial for each of the characters.
Apart from story mode, there are challenges waiting to be completed and a multiplayer mode in which you can play against other people (both locally and online). With 6 modes available in local multiuplayer, It's quite fun to play during a party, but be aware that it might not keep you excited for long.
As I mentioned befeore, BRAWL is extremely difficult and will punish you almost every time you are too slow or make a stupid mistake. In theory, you can load the last checkpoint when you fail, but there aren't many of them, so you usually start the whole level from scratch anyway. It can be very frustrating, especially during those unfair bossfights that can take even up to 15 minutes to complete if you're unlucky.

At first I thought this would end up being just a Bomberman clone with a dark and gritty setting. Turns out this is actually a creative and interesting take on the Bomberman formula with much more strategy involved. For example, every character has a special and an ability. The girl with the bear as an example can throw a knife with one button and teleport to and/or trade places with it with another button. It is a very intriguing usage of the formula with enough differences to stand on its own two feet. There are of course powerups like in Bomberman, but interestingly the more pickups the character gets, the more they charge up to ultimately use their Ultra ability. The girl's ultra is a very fast and infinite range bomb explosion that can wipe out enemies quickly if used properly. Another neat feature they have included in the game is that you can stack up to two lives via picking up health powerups so if you get hit, you can keep going which can make a world of difference. There are even cool little touches such as indicators on the ground under your character to indicate exactly which square you are on so you know if you will be hit by explosions. There are also visual indicators on the ground showing how far a bomb's blast will go so you can avoid it. Also interestingly, there is a Story mode where the stories of these different dark and gritty characters is told by what seems to be the owner of the Emporium who teaches you their abilities, and also about their personalities and ideas for how to use them. The Story Mode is also fun and strategic due to having to deal with minions and also at times a main enemy such as a boss or other opponent. I am greatly enjoying the game so far and I love the fact that this is a Bomberman-like game with an atmosphere and grittiness of something nearly like Twisted Metal with grim and dark story telling. Also the sound, music, and voice acting are great and puts you into the character and mood of the game. One thing to mention is that the boss fights (in Story Mode) can be quite challenging and can be difficult to survive and come out on top. I suppose though, that the point of a boss fight in most games is to make it difficult and challenging for the player. Overall, I love and highly recommend this game to everyone that loves Bomberman and games like it looking for a very dark, clever, and strategic twist to the formula!

I bought this title because I loved the fresh concept behind Stanley Parable, and thought its quirky execution was charming.
This title is NOT like Stanley Parable. It's not polished, it barely has any game mechanic. Although it does have a story, it's definitely not fun, and mostly it's not even aesthetically pleasing or well-made.
I would argue that this isn't even a game. It's a short biography of a game designer named Coda, illustrated with examples of his work, and bound together with a voice-over by his friend, the "game"'s director.
It's a deeply personal project, and unless you have any topical or stylistic connection with the works of Devey or Coda, I don't recommend buying it. If Coda was a famous and accomplished game designer, this would be a neat biography about his early works. But as such, it's not only unfit for public consumption, it may actually be illegal. If the narrated story is true, Coda explicitly prohibits his friend from publishing his works, and yet this collection is offered commercially on Steam.

Alright this game is not bad. Definitely fun to gather three friends at max and just have some fun. The loot as I saw a few say was good I disagree with because 90% of the loot I get is garbage but the game is still fun. To make it short and sweet there is four classes each with only four abilites and four traps/towers. The focus is destroying waves of enemies as they go towards a main structure to defend. Basically you and your friends are playing a tower defense game together while also being able to attack the monsters with a 3rd person view character. One thing I don't really like is that all of the classes get a "serious" look but the Squire I believe is the name or the knight as some refer to him.. well he has this dumb outfit and you cannot change it unless you pay real money. He would be fine if the other characters had a more childish theme but he has smiley faces on his wooden swords and shields. For me it is just odd that he sticks out so much as a random silly character while the others get weapons that seem more fitting for battle. Another thing though is the limit on the amount of tower/traps you can build plus the lack of mana to even build them in the first place. If you are online and a player sweeps in and steals all the mana on the ground and builds as many towers as he can to tier 1 so that you cannot build anything well it kind of sucks. They should increase the max defense limit by at least 3 or 4 just so that others can have at least 2 defenses instead of one. The mana is mostly given to the Squire as he is up close and can pick it all up... giving him a much larger advantage at getting the defenses he wants. I don't know maybe it is just me the game is still a ton of fun and if you just want a game to fool around in with a few friends some night then get this game and some fun.

Easily belongs to the top 10 puzzle games of all time. And if the word "puzzle game" might not sound like your cup of tea, don't worry, this game knows how to keep you glued in for another level to solve with its story and dark humor.
The first levels might seem a breeze, to a point where you'll go "pfft, this isn't that hard", But gradually you'll be confronted with challenges where your brain will start melting. Once you do find a solution that works however, the feeling is really satisfying.
The further you progress in the levels, the more the solutions become "yours" because there's more than one way to solve a puzzle. If you're curious how well you did, at the end of each level you can compare your score with other players.
Dare I even say that this game is analogous with programming. Every programmer's brain works differently and will have a different approach to each task, eventually their code will do the same operation, but one will be more efficient and/or shorter than the other.
To sum up, it's a fun puzzle game that will probably make you cry from sadness, frustration and happiness all at the same time.

UT remains a classic multiplayer FPS that continues to influence game creators to this day. When it was released, Epic Games was competing with id Software for the FPS crown. Both companies decided to focus on multiplayer, with offline play supported by bots. While id's Quake 3: Arena went with stripped-down gameplay polished to a high sheen, Epic crammed in as many features and game modes as they could.
Besides the standard Deathmatch and CTF modes, UT introduced new modes like Assault that focused heavily on team-based action. Mutators that changed different aspects of the gameplay could be applied to any match and added lots of variety. Each weapon had a primary and secondary mode, which greatly increased the strategies available with each one. And while UT had the standard corridor-based Deathmatch maps, it also had huge open maps that were a sniper's dream, and many of them were larger than had ever been seen in a FPS at he time.
The classic gameplay still holds up, though most players gravitate to the game's successor, UT2K4, which took everything good about UT and cranked it up to 11 while adding many more unique features. If you want to see where modern shooters have their roots, UT is a great place to start playing.

Infinifactory is a game where you build machinery (like an assembly line in a factory) to transform blocks you are provided with into goal objects.  As with other Zachtronics games, you are scored in several ways based on your solution: cycles (the amount of time your solution takes,) footprint (the amount of floor space your solution takes up,) and blocks (the number of blocks you use.)
You are provided with various blocks to move objects, attach them to eachother, or destroy them along with some blocks for logic operations.  Put them together, and you can build some pretty complex machines from these simple parts.  It's a very intuitive system, and never overwhelming.  Problems can be broken down into small parts which are easy to solve (and these segments are often quite similar between puzzles.)  There's always something you can do to try to make a machine work if it's not quite there yet, no walls you run into where you feel like you can't continue.  When everything does finally come together at the end of a complicated and lengthy puzzle, it's very satisfying watching your solution run to completion.
I'd also like to personally thank Zach (the developer.)  I was having issues with random crashing and when I sent in a bug report, he responded with a couple hours with a solution (turns out it was my cloud storage software causing a conflict with the save file, not a bug in the game.)
Back to slaving away building factories for the alien overlords!

I really liked Napoleon Total War.  It is one of my favorite total war games, along with Shogun 2.
Things I liked:
I like the individual city based approach as opposed to the newer 3 cities in a province approach.
I'm a fan of the Napoleonic era, and have played many strategic boardgames set in this timeframe.   This game has a similar feel to Empires in Arms, and other strategic Napoleon era games.
I like the cav vs. artillery, infantry vs. cav, artillery vs. infantry matchups.
AI for all computer games is somewhat suspect.  This AI is ok on defense, but lacking on offense.  For best results, the player should be on offense and the computer AI on defense.
The objectives and victory conditions are good.
Technology tree is ok, but nothing special.
I've played several campaigns: Egypt, Italian, and Grand Campaign (1805-1812, both Napoleon or an allied power (UK, Russian, etc.).  My preference is the grand campaign because of diplomacy, trade, technology, etc., but the other campaigns are also pretty good.
Really nice game for your free time.

The game needs a serious upgrade in inventory management and inventory presentation.
The complete lack of a paper-doll inventory (like dayz has it) and inventory being represented by a drop down list is very damaging to the survival experience. It is very tedious to repeatedly work through a drop down list harvest and repair items. It feels completely detached from the game and it is as fun as interacting with a spreadsheet.
The same problem carries over into looting. While the visual feel of searchinga house with a lit match is a lot of fun, looting of items is not. Having to loot a desk with multiple drawers is tedious as hell because it is all progress bars and no visual item to pick up (unlike items in shelves).
I hope the developers invest some time into a real inventory system like DAYZ has it. DAYZ set the standard for survival game inventories and GONE HOME for looting items out of furniture. Right now looting and crafting is a very tedious task. It would be bad if that remains like that because it drags the game down.

FRIDAY NIGHT BULLET ARENA is a top-down multiplayer shoot-a-thon with a twist: each player only gets one bullet! You can catch your own bullet to fire again and other's bullets kill you!

-Gameplay-
Local Multiplayer only game, where 2-4 players go into space to kill each other. Ultra simplistic mechanics, either using the RS for the Xbox controller or A,B,Y,X to shoot a bullet, only one bullet per player in this small arena top down shooter to kill your opponent. First one to get to 16 kills will be declared the winner.
-Graphics, Sound & Artstyle-
FNBA has a very forgetable artstyle, sometimes I forgot I the setting I was playing in even if I'm a HUGE fan of what it was meant to be playing in. The soundtrack and characters for me was what saved the game's aesthetic for me. Quirky characters with fun names and ambient music made it enjoyable
-Price-
The retail price is 9.99 USD
-How many hours estimated?-
It's a fun little indie game to play with friends, but the lack of bots and heavier emphasis on more players equaling more fun really brings it's stock down for me. I estimate playing this for about 5-6 hours.

-Buy it Now? Wait for Sale? Don't Buy?-
While I personally had fun with the game, FNBA is a local multiplayer game that hurts a lot for not having online. Theres content a plenty there to keep one playing for hours, but the fact that it plays better with 3-4 players much better is what is dissapointing. Even a bot would help it a lot here. I will be recommending it as
just because of the small tidbits. Someone like myself could take advantage of everything this game has to offer, but people who don't have many friends to come over and play with will not have a good time with it because of the price of 9.99USD. At 2.99 USD I would recommend this game 100% as BUY IT NOW!

This is very good at the moment. Knowing what anime online multiplayer games with in-game purchases are like, it might not always be good - so get in quick if you like TCGs.
You play with a hand of 12 cards that you choose from your collection, and 5 can be on the board at a time. So the strategy of what orders and locations to play the cards is more important than in games where the cards are drawn at random. Most cards operate via a special effect rather than damage - and as well as synergies with the other cards in your deck, the way your synergies interact with what cards the opponent happens to have chosen matters. It so tightly balanced that I'm tempted to print off hard copies of the cards and play on a table - before the game develops power creep or turns into a cash-grab or the playerbase dies.
Some cards are overpowered, some players are overpowered, some card combinations are overpowered - but after playing a few dozen matches most people are rely on common cards (from a pool of about 200 familiar ones) and they might have one rare one that they bring out as a finisher. Cards in tier 4 and tier 5 have low drop rates, players who spend real money will have more of those to choose from - but they still need to know how to use them, and you might be lucky and happen to have brought a combination of common cards that perfectly exploits their weaknesses. I like that you can't really grind for cards - it is a gold and gems system - only common cards can be bought with gold, and you can only grind enough gems a day for 10-15 cards, maybe an hour, or 2 hours if also doing the tutorial.
The single-player campaign which also stands as the tutorial is awesome - it has about 100 set-ups where you have to beat the computer using strange combinations, such as how to win with no damage-dealing cards. Between each of these matches you get a bit of storyline - and it is genius, it's almost worth playing just to watch it. Heck it's worth a few hours of anyone's time to see the card artwork they did for the Kobold Power Rangers.
Most of the time there are enough people playing to find a match - not much chat or social interaction (which I prefer). People seem to gravitate to ordinary duels more than the events (which have a similar format to Senran Kagura's Japanese mobile site). When the population is low there is the option to play against bots using real players' card hands while you wait for a real player to come up in the queue. You can always be pretty sure of beating the AI - but you at least get to figure out how to beat it, depending on what cards it has.
A lucky find - come play it while it is good.

I have really tried to give this game the benefit of the doubt and play further before a review that might be unfair, but I simply cannot tolerate it anymore.  This game is WAY overpriced for what you get, and is worth only $10 when NOT on sale in my opinion.
The best way to sum up this game is mediocre.  The story is truly pathetic, if you can call it a story at all, and the writing and dialogue are hands down the worst I have ever seen in a game that isn't TRYING to be BBB rated.  The story is 100% linear in every way, there is no exploration of any kind (unless you consider opening up every nook on a small map exploring), and every mission is exactly the same.  There isn't truly a world map, as you are always going on what they call "raids" into small maps that you port to.  These maps are small, uninspired, terrible to repeat, and are not connected.  You will have to find several of a few types of items to get resources to upgrade the armorsmith, weaponsmith, etc. in your town.  Note, this cannot happen when you want since you must play through certain missions to get the required materials, and they force you to upgrade different buildings in a certain order.  You have to try and kill multiple enemies/monsters simultaneously to get the most "blood" (which is gathered in order to make a sacrifice and level), and you will simply clear a map, open a certain number of treasure chests to ensure you get all of that map's resources, and then kill a final boss that may or may not be difficult.  Regardless of how difficult you find it, you will be doing NOTHING but buttom smashing and roll dodging (which usually doesn't prevent damage or enable a more powerful attack).  You will repeat this exact scenario until you can no longer survive and attack because you must upgrade a building and make new armor and weapons.  It is a predictable rhythm that is unoriginal at best, and tedious at worst.
But it gets worse.  The maps offer environmental effects called exposure.  Some examples of this are cold and poison areas that are on a timer.  If you stay in the area past the timer on your bar you begin to take that type of damage.  To prevent the damage you have to either get into a safe area, or stand near a fire until the timer runs back down.  Now you might be thinking this is innnovative or something, but let me assure you it is not.  What is does is basically add an element of annoyance.  It does not increase difficulty, it does not increase reward, it does not require thinking or strategy; all it does is annoy you and cause you to have to do extra running back and forth in the same areas.
The music has its moments where it is decent, but many times it is either annoying or sounds like it was created in a high school student's garage.  It does little for the atmosphere or mood, unless they were going for uninspired and annoying.  Add to the music the fact that your character is rather obnoxious, and never shuts up with statements like, "You couldn't even touch me!" or "I cannot be defeated!"  ad infinitum.
The graphics aren't bad, but they aren't revolutionary or any better than any other modern game of this type.
I just cannot find anything good to say about this game.  I suppose that if you have played all games of this type, live for them, and need something new then you could try this, but if you play $39 for it you have been ripped off so be warned.  I do NOT recommend this game.

I was really excited about Outlast. I'm pretty stingy when it comes to games, so I naturally waited until it came on sale. Sadly, my high expectations for it weren't met.
The visuals and audio in the game are stellar. I don't have a high end computer, but it ran perfectly on high graphics settings. The animations were smooth. Typically in a first-person game I don't like the animations the creators give the hands of the character - either climbing walls, running, ect. These are smooth, combined with a slight sway of the screen when walking. Normally, to me, things like that in a game feel gimmicky and unperfected, but it works beautifully in Outlast.
The actual gameplay is where it gets me. I enjoyed it for a short while, then the tasks started becoming repetitive. Often times, a quest will appear that I wouldn't actually /want/ to do if I was in that situation. That takes me both out of the world of Outlast and turns it into a game that's not nearly as enjoyable and repetitive.
The scares are good. The game is full of creepy things. Jump scares are a large part of it, but not nearly all of it. I found myself tensed up in several situations.
That being said, some of the content in the game, I felt, went a little "too far". I'm extrodinarily picky when it comes to horror games and movies, becuase I find gore, when used as a tactic for scares, as an "easy way out". For example - when playing Outlast, you'll find yourself in hundreds of different rooms and hallways with blood, corpses hanging from the ceilings, ect. I don't mind it. However, from a player's persepective, I found that to be a little "too much". When everything is hyped up to be the most nasty gore-fest imaginable, it loses a little bit of the shock value. I understand that the premise is of an asylum gone wrong, but I still can't get over the setting. From a "scary game" or movie persepective, I would enjoy something closer to F3AR or the movie I Am Legend. Outlast is very atmospheric, and that creepy atmosphere is more than enough to give someone the heebie-jeebies.
Also, the having sex with a dead body thing is a little off too.
In conclusion, Outlast is a solid game. I love scary games and being frightened out of my wits. However, Outlast just doesn't hit home for me. I feel that overall it's a little repetitive, a little gimmicky, and it has it's moments when you're taken completely out of the story. Buy it if it's on sale for a couple hours worth of scares. :)
Finally, a survival game that isn't plagued with trolls or gankers. Who need's zombies and PvP when you have strong winds and no socks!

Note: I played the game for a short time only and while exploring was fun so far, the inventory system is a massive drag on the fun, so I do not recommend the game in its current state
The game needs a serious upgrade in inventory management and inventory presentation.
The complete lack of a paper-doll inventory (like dayz has it) and inventory being represented by a drop down list is very damaging to the survival experience. Interacting with the inventory is a chore, because if I want to eat something I have to click through 2 menus and a drop down list. With crafting it is even worse. It is very tedious to repeatedly work through a drop down list harvest and repair items. It feels completely detached from the game and it is as fun as interacting with a spreadsheet.
The same problem carries over into looting. While the visual feel of searchinga house with a lit match is a lot of fun, looting of items is not. Having to loot a desk with multiple drawers is tedious as hell because it is all progress bars and no visual item to pick up (unlike items in shelves).
I hope the developers invest some time into a real inventory system like DAYZ has it. DAYZ set the standard for survival game inventories and GONE HOME for looting items out of furniture. Right now looting and crafting is a very tedious task. It would be bad if that remains like that because it drags the game down.
And before the DAYZ haters come in, keep in mind the current asking price for TLD and DAYZ is almost the same so these games are directly comparable in the inventory representation

I do recommend this but there's something I have to warn you about first. Do not, under any circumstances, use ANY of the stock content or any of their expansion packs (the ones created by developers). Yes these packs were created by professional artists and musicians, but do you think you're the only one using them? Every single sprite, every single mechanic, every single sound that is in those packs is likely being used by hundreds of other people hoping to make a game with RPG Maker. The only game that benefits from these packs is the first person to use them in an actual game.
Only use custom-designed content either made yourself or bought from someone else.
Aside from this point, it's a fairly functional game development program. You can mod and edit the source code to accomodate your own needs a little more if you wish, but unless you're good at the programming language (or have a natural lingual talent and can learn the language very quickly) I don't recommend it. The stock engine is fairly versatile and you can make a lot of headway with it alone if you need to otherwise. But if you're making a game using any stock or expansion sprites, portraits, icons, or sounds... well... don't bother trying to charge people for it or you'll be laughed out of greenlight.

A classic and still my favorite Unreal title, the original Unreal Tournament is a marvel of gaming excellence and is a benchmark other deathmatch shooters should strive to meet.  My first encounter with this game was on the PS2 and this GotY Steam version is only better, so if you've ever played this game you should definitely pick up this improved version.  The gameplay is just as good as it always has been and hasn't added any unnecessary complexity with the GotY tag.  Its simplicity is what makes it so awesome, and this version is a prime example of that.  I could add that Mod support is built into the engine, the settings are excellent for such an old title, the gameplay is crisp, clean, and fast, the sound quality is superb...I could go on and on, but there shouldn't be any reason to.  If you like Multiplayer / Arena FPS you know what Unreal Tournament is and if you haven't played the original you're missing out on the game that defined the genre.  There are Quake fans, there are Unreal fans, there are Halo fans, and even Call of Duty fans, but all gamers can appreciate the history of the medium and the titles that laid the groundwork for the future, and Unreal Tournament is undeniably THE title that brought these types of games to the forefront of gaming culture.
Pick it up for nostalgia's sake or even pick it up because it's still the best arena shooter created to date, Unreal Tournament is a game no FPS (or gaming) fan should lack and is just as fun today as when it hit the shelves all those years ago.
A+, do not miss.

It's a very personal game, that I can say for sure. Heavily introspective and will not provide straight answers to the questions it poses. If you'd like a trip into Davey Wreden's personal conflict with the desire to make and the making itself, step in. It's definitely worth the asking price. If you're looking for The Stanley Parable, this game has very little of the humour and all of the philosophical crises. This game isn't about games and players. It's about making games, but mostly self-expression in making anything.
PS: Check out the company's website, and find in it the link to the talk Davey gave in Helsinki. It might help with this game, prior or after playing it. Preferably after, I guess.
Edit: It seems that many people are trying to find out how it compares to The Stanley Parable, so here it is: it's not TSP at all. TSP is cynical, hilarious, and scatterbrained to some extent. This game is painfully earnest, scary, and has only one question in its core. In my opinion, it is the better game, but it's not for everyone. (Mind, I'm the kind of guy who thinks MGS2 is better than 3, even if the game in 3 is better than 2. Make of that what you will.)

Binary reductionist "Reviews" are but one (limited) way to understand modern digital interactive art experiences - like The Beginner's Guide. (Perhaps a more useful response would be to make another game oneself?) It seems developer Davey Wreden has as much idea about what's going here on as anyone else. And that's neither a good or bad thing - nor both. What then is there to recommend (andor not recommend) The Beginner's Guide? The beginner's guide to what?
Player-Researcher X: Exactly!
Player-Researcher Y: What?
Playing (/with) this game and others like it, one feels it was some odd non-thing Vladimir and Estragon mashed up while waiting for 'Coda' to show up. With The Beginner's Guide, this "(Apparently) 4th wall breaking meta-game" trope is now even more fully developed - and seems no less theoretically problematic to discuss than before, even for its admirers.
Or should that be forever potential admirers (since they, like the devs have little *but* endless ideas regarding whatever such games might potentially mean)? Indeed, this game and The Stanley Parable are like the Zero Point Energy of modern (contested) game development negative-space..
Anyway, I personally decided to purchase this Walking Simulator (say it out loud - stand short and stride forth incrementally, fellow slow motion hikers!) because.. actually I don't really know. "It seemed OK." The lighting and overall atmosphere are particularly effective; a diffuse ambient meanings-field. That's about all I can say right now. (I've not yet had enough coffee today.) I'll probably put up a more detailed critique on my site at some point.
Thanks for listening to this unorthodox (yet defective) semi-review.

If you enjoyed The Stanley Parable, Gone Home, Dear Esthar, or similar games that are about walking through an environment, and particularly, about game design, then the journey provided by The Beginner's Guide (and what really does the titling of the game mean in context? Difficult to say) will be one that leaves you astounded, breathless, weepy, and proud at the same time.
As an aside: you will learn about the vulnerability of artists, two in fact, who might be closer than we realize. The game explores the dynamics of game design, first by explaining, through a variety of less complex ideas to more complex ideas what game design means to people, how stripping away the AAA traditions gets closer to the heart of the thing.
It's these indie titles that spur the most creative thinking in game design, and the reality is that this will be a more designed experience than it offers you and us. It will play at being criticism of another when it's slowly trying to point out how personal everything, including advice, criticism, and love really are.
Please, play this game. It will affect you if you have an open mind or a love for the video game genre. It is easily a must play.

Abilities: Each hero only has 4 towers and abilities. D1 had more. So your forced into certain playstyles and gearing.
Stats: there are plenty of stats to choose from but only 3-4 stats are worth getting.
Scaling: they really tuned down the scaling so you can't stat up in unique ways.
Every map feels and plays the same, wall-tower
Focus? seems like the devs just want a good basic core game at the moment and balance, but this isn't MLG or in any way competitive, why not give some fun customization with stats at early levels?

Just Cause 2 review:
I might not have played this game for some 150+ hours on this account, but trust me, I would have around 125 by now, most of which spent free-roaming. But let's just get straight to the game!
In JC2, the graphics are breath-taking, although they do take quite a good computer to handle on decent settings. I have an extremely good PC that can run most games on high settings with 55-60fps, same with this game, until you look at Anti-Aliasing. Just by turning the AA higher than 4X, it only gives me 30fps, you can clearly tell how much work has been put into this wonderful game already. But apart from that, the explosions are absolutely amazing, the destruction engine if awesome, therefore, most of the games graphics are beautiful! Although Avalanche Studios didn't put as much love underwater, you can only see Rico (main character), the sea ground, and a very awkard blue mist.But keep in mind, this game is now quite old, so it was like a GTA V for it's time, and it still remains as awesome as ever.
The gameplay is just... too good for words to be honest! The free-roaming actually suits  its purpose in Just Cause 2! You can either go into a mission, free roam, use the Black Market Chopper for different actions or just mod the game. You can probably do anything in the free roam stage, even blow up an enemy base, steal a vehicle, or try and sneakily assassinate a Colonel. There's always something to do, such as upgrade a weapon, find all the secrets, hijack all the vehicles and play with friends on multiplayer. The multiplayer isn't horrible, but it's not excellent either, first of all, it can get boring quite easily, second of all of all, not a lot of people play it anymore, but that's about it for it's cons. There isn't any type of editor (as far as I'm aware of), so you can't make a new island, a new Rico costume, or even a simple reskin! That is a feature tons of game should add, but sadly JC2 doesn't, so we can only hope that JC3 does. So if you do get bored, try out some mods for your entertainment.

The missions are not as bad as people say, at least that's my opinion. I do prefer to just free roam rather than do missions, though. Some of the missions are a let down, but others are quite enjoyable. They could've been so much better, but hey, you can't argue if you look at the rest of the game. Missions do feel a bit... "thrown in" to the game, as if they just said, "let's build a few bases and make the players assassinate the Colonels or destroy those bases". To back this up, I have to say this, they make you travel to the locations while trying to manouver the terrain and other obstacles to make you appriciate how much work they put into the detail on every single road.
This is quite a wierd topic, but Just Cause 2 has some really great and High Quality sounds! Most of which are explosions. The few soundtracks are absolutely awesome, I would pay to see more of the soundtracks in the game. Most things have their own sound, which proves my point even further about this game of awe and wonder!  The guns don't have such excellent sounds as I would've wanted them too, so that's hopefully going to be improved in JC3. But that's about it for sound, it's mostly great, but nothing is terrible.
Yes, as long as you don't really care too much about missions or sound quality, but you're safe if you don't in this game. So for most people, this game is a clean yes.

The industry is rife with "survival games" which dissolve into zombie simulators full of infinite ammo and head smashing. It was fun, sure, and we enjoyed it while it lasted, but the time has come for us to stop worrying about the end of the world being filled with the undead-- what about the living, breathing world we are enveloped by?
Just from the Sandbox experience, I was thrilled to discover a survival situation replete with many elements ignored by other similar games. Real danger from the environment and its wildlife, the threat of starvation, dehydration, and untreated wounds, etc., I could go on. This game has come the closest to realism in a game of its type while abstracting many tasks to permit ease of play and learning. Tasks cost time, calories, and heat, impressing upon the player the need to critically monitor their resources--when you are out of wood, suddenly that pack of matches doesn't look so promising.
If multiplayer was included in future versions, I have no doubt it could rival DayZ for content and feel based on this alpha alone! Especially if the environment could be augmented to be harsher for multiple players, and the players are set to work collabortively against the winter and wolves. That could be amazing, and the first game to focus on sheer survivability in place of how players can kill each other off for their goods.
I look forward to the future of this game, having already caught my interest and earned my enthusiasm.
EDIT: When I first wrote this, I made an incredible newbie oversight. I didn't know about the Survival Panel (TAB). On triggering this accidentally, I realized the game easily allowed me to to do the things I had complained about be unable to do (make a fire wherever, find fuel for fire, etc.). Major oversight on my part. Having discovered and tested the feel with this feature being applied, I loved it all the more.

I was intrigued by the trailer and its premise and I am so glad I picked this game up when it went on sale. This is arguably  the most authentic to real life game I have ever played, yet its captivating because of how well it plays off the feeling of being completly isolated and cutoff from any kind of help.
Just take a second to appreciate that, you have a game here that has pretty much zero fantasy elements(aside from the absurdly aggressive wolves(I dont know, maybe they're starving in an overly harsh winter)) yet it manages to be more terrifying than a lot of conventional horror games once you get immersed in it.
With most conventional horror monsters theres a gimmick that you can control, stare at it or dont stare at it, stay in the light or dont. In this game your foe is winter itself. Warface has been one of the funnest games ive played in a long time. The assist mechanic has to be my favourite thing about the game as it provides a feel of teamwork required when playing the game. The 4 classes (engineer, sniper, medic and riflemen) all have their ups and downs depending on what map is chosen making all the classes equal in what I call 'overpoweredness'. Personaly my favourite class is the sniper class because of the most-of-the-time one shot kill snipers. However, despite saying possitive things about the game, it has its downsides. For me there are only 2 things i dislike about the game. 1) The ranking system. One you reach around lvl 13 or so, you are able to go against lvl 82 players (currently the highest lvl in the game) and under which makes it really unfair to most players that want to enjoy the game. 2) The gun rental system. Most of the really good weapons in the game can only be rented for a period of time such as 2 hours 1 day or 1 week. This forces you to re-buy the weapons once their rental expires. This takes up alot of WD (warface dollars) and it doesent include the hefty price required to repair them once their durability wears down. Considering the cost to repair your equiped and unequiped equipment such as weapons and armor adding to the repair cost of the rented guns is going to cost a huge amount of WD. The regular repair costs are already considered to be expensive and it gets more expensive the less durability the weapon or armor has. Those 2 things are the only thing I dislike in Warface. WDs are easy to earn during missions. There are a good variety of missions from the average TDM (team deathmatch) to something called Storm which you have to find out what it is yourself by playing the game. Winning a game of storm gives you the most WDs and is also my favourite gamemode to play. If you do not feel like playing against other players and you are more fond of campaign kind of missions, warface although not having a campaign, has a co-op pve mode where you and your friends or a group of random players play missions against enemy AI completing various objectives. This can go up to 4 players and can be really fun when playing with friends. The only downside to that is that if you want to play with friends the lobby MUST contain 4 players in order to start the mission. All in all, Warface is 102% worth downloading and playing. It is a free to play game that feels like a paid game. This is the most fun FPS game ive played in a very long time. A question my friends would ask me is, CSGO or Warface? Right now I would deffinitely choose Warface over CSGO and keep in mind, i have 4.7k hours in CSGO im basicaly addicted to the game but Warface has broken that addiction and now I might get addicted to Warface instead.

When I bought this game I was not sure what I expected. The highly popular Stanley Parable with its incredibly sophisticated and deep narrative was a blast. So, like many other I thought: this is a game by one of the creators of one of my most favorite games of all times. I didn't care that you can finish the Beginner's Guide in about one and a half hours. Neither did I expect an action packed shooter, or an engaging thriller. The only thing I wanted was a story...
Let me tell you right now, this is what I got! An captivating emotional journey. It is both simple in gameplay and hard to understand. The Beginner's Guide attempts to understand a person through seeing (and playing) his work. Davey  Wreden leads the player through the weird games of his unknown game designer friend "Coda" and shares his interpreation of what the player experiences. On this path through various small games an image of this Coda begins to form in your head. You'll think you know this mysterious man, who is working on games, but never shows them to anyone.
You'll run through mazes, chasing after Coda, maybe Wreden, or maybe even yourself. This game is as much a game as it is not. It addresses you on meta-levels beyond anything I thought was possible and from chapter to chapter I could feel myself shifting through emotions. Sometimes gradually, sometimes instantly.
When I was done playing The Beginner's Guide I was torn. For a very long moment it left me empty in a limbo of my own thoughts. What should I think of this? Was the story they told me the true thing? Were that intimite thoughts of Wreden or a scripted plot he followed right to every small detail? Does this Coda exist? I am not sure. Yet I would not care either way.
In my opinion The Beginner's Guide is an indie masterpiece and deserves nothing less than the most attention possible. This game made me happy and made me want to cry. It was inspiring and disconcerting. The deep message of the game touched me in a certain way. I felt connected to both Wreden and Coda, none of whom I know. It was more than I expected and everything I hoped for. Elaborate thoughts about a person you do not know were presented in a way that the player thinks he might understand. Even though he probably can not.
Should you be a fan of action or intaractivity, someone who does not want to think about much while playing a game, then The Beginner's Guide is not for you. However if you are searching for answers, about others and maybe yourself. Or if you like an engaging, emotional, simple, artistic, appealing, deep, and meta game than you should definitely check this game out.
In my opinion it is one of the greatest thought-provoking games out there. It was worth every cent. To me Wreden will be known as one of the best game designers ever from here on out. I am looking forward to more games like this and will  keep thinking about The Beginner's Guide many years to come.

I finished this game about an hour ago and I still feel a mix of being both emotionally charged and emotionally drained. If you like games that make you feel something, then you will like this. Don't look up anything more about the game until you have finished it. You need to experience it as something completely new and unknown. It will only take you about an hour and a half to complete, but I have a feeling it will stay with you indefinitely, so I don't consider it a short game for that reason.
It's very different from the Stanley Parable, but if I didn't know it was made by the same person, I would've linked back to it. There is a similar feeling of unease to both games. Sort of like an outer body experience. But where the Stanley Parable has a lot of humour and light heartedness, the Beginner's Guide feels intensly sad and desperate. And it really did make me feel that way. There were parts of the game that made me want to throw up, and other parts which I played with a constant stream of tears on my face. It was a solid visual interpretation of anxiety and depression.
Don't go into this game expecting the Stanley Parable 2. I think that's where a lot of the negative reviews come from. This game has one ending, and there aren't places where you can change things or veer off track. If the game tells you to do something, it won't progress until you do the thing. And it's more like an ineractive movie than a game. You are simply listening to a story while you walk around the scenery. There will be people who won't like the game for that reason. And there are other people who will find it hugely effective and immersive, as I did.
If you have finished it, here is my interpretation. (And please please please only read this if you have finished playing.)
That's my take on the game. Everyone else's interpretation might be very different, but I think that's partly the point of it. It was a very charged insight into the human condition, and I loved it. I would love to hear other people's interpretations too.

As I'm only 30 minutes in, this review will be a basic impression of the port itself.
Overall, it's relatively solid for a Japanese dev. It's got a good range of resolution options, even going up to 1440p for my monitor. Preset graphics selections, FXAA support, draw distance, and a few other things to modify for graphics on top of that. It runs smoothly without any signs of stutters or crashing.
The biggest caveat for some would be the ugly textures in places and 30 FPS lock. However, I'm able to forgive them as it's a port of a PS3 game.  Allowing higher than 30 FPS would have broken the combat system, according to the developers.
Still, hopefully with this game successful, they'll see PC as not a place to port, but as a primary release for future Tales games. And maybe those games will be designed around 60 FPS from the get go.
For the game itself, I can't judge. Only 30 minutes in. But so far, it seems to bring the standard Tales flavour, with its own unique charm.  If you love Tales games, you'll love this game.
EDIT: After 3 hours of playing today, I've experienced a few graphical issues. Screen tearing and flickering happens extremely rarely, but it's noticeable when it does. However, this happaned maybe once an hour.
The battle camera can also be an issue: But only in the specific instance of battle starting while you're in a cramped area (like a doorway).
Still, these two problems are not nearly enough for me to not recommend it. In those 3 hours, most of my experience was good. The battle system is deep, and a good flow of tutorials and new mechanics means that it won't get stale for awhile - even once they stop I'll still have a lot to learn.

I've played this a pretty decent amount and this is what I can say so far.
1. The mechanics are a lot of fun. The game is very interesting compare to your typical card game. You don't get unlimited actions per turn and your resources don't fill up to max per turn. This is very fresh..
2. It's a TCG, not a CCG. This means that players can trade with other players and buy/sell from/to each other. This makes it easier to get entire playsets or specific cards. This means that the game is not P2W at all.
3. Nexon is very generous with rewards.
Now.. why I don't recommend playing this game "right now" is due to the playerbase. The playerbase is very small and they mainly play between 7:00 am PDT and 9:00 am PDT. Most of the playerbase is from Asia. This means that if you don't play during this window, you won't get many, if any, ranked matches. You can play casual mode with the other people from the US, sure. You just won't get to play any monthly ranked, weekly ranked, or weekend ranked. I don't know why US players don't play those modes and only people from Asia do, but w/e, it is what it is and that means only 1 match every 6-9 hours if you don't play during those 2 hours when the people from Asia are on. Also, you can be sure that your rare matches are going to be people from Asia, like Japan.
Anyways, continue to check steamcharts if you are interested and wait for the playerbase to be more substantial beyond the hours of 7:00 am PDT to 9:00 am PDT. It doesn't matter if it grows only during that timeframe =P.
I also need to note that the OST is horrible, the UI is horrible, and that the first impression couldn't be worse.

Just Cause 2 review:
I might not have played this game for some 150+ hours on this account, but trust me, I would have around 125 by now, most of which spent free-roaming. But let's just get straight to the game!
In JC2, the graphics are breath-taking, although they do take quite a good computer to handle on decent settings. I have an extremely good PC that can run most games on high settings with 55-60fps, same with this game, until you look at Anti-Aliasing. Just by turning the AA higher than 4X, it only gives me 30fps, you can clearly tell how much work has been put into this wonderful game already. But apart from that, the explosions are absolutely amazing, the destruction engine if awesome, therefore, most of the games graphics are beautiful! Although Avalanche Studios didn't put as much love underwater, you can only see Rico (main character), the sea ground, and a very awkard blue mist.But keep in mind, this game is now quite old, so it was like a GTA V for it's time, and it still remains as awesome as ever.
The gameplay is just... too good for words to be honest! The free-roaming actually suits  its purpose in Just Cause 2! You can either go into a mission, free roam, use the Black Market Chopper for different actions or just mod the game. You can probably do anything in the free roam stage, even blow up an enemy base, steal a vehicle, or try and sneakily assassinate a Colonel. There's always something to do, such as upgrade a weapon, find all the secrets, hijack all the vehicles and play with friends on multiplayer. The multiplayer isn't horrible, but it's not excellent either, first of all, it can get boring quite easily, second of all of all, not a lot of people play it anymore, but that's about it for it's cons. There isn't any type of editor (as far as I'm aware of), so you can't make a new island, a new Rico costume, or even a simple reskin! That is a feature tons of game should add, but sadly JC2 doesn't, so we can only hope that JC3 does. So if you do get bored, try out some mods for your entertainment.

The missions are not as bad as people say, at least that's my opinion. I do prefer to just free roam rather than do missions, though. Some of the missions are a let down, but others are quite enjoyable. They could've been so much better, but hey, you can't argue if you look at the rest of the game. Missions do feel a bit... "thrown in" to the game, as if they just said, "let's build a few bases and make the players assassinate the Colonels or destroy those bases". To back this up, I have to say this, they make you travel to the locations while trying to manouver the terrain and other obstacles to make you appriciate how much work they put into the detail on every single road.
This is quite a wierd topic, but Just Cause 2 has some really great and High Quality sounds! Most of which are explosions. The few soundtracks are absolutely awesome, I would pay to see more of the soundtracks in the game. Most things have their own sound, which proves my point even further about this game of awe and wonder!  The guns don't have such excellent sounds as I would've wanted them too, so that's hopefully going to be improved in JC3. But that's about it for sound, it's mostly great, but nothing is terrible.
Yes, as long as you don't really care too much about missions or sound quality, but you're safe if you don't in this game. So for most people, this game is a clean yes.

Original review:
Here's how the experience was for me:
I purchased this game even though it was out of my budget, because I thought it would deliver what it promised to be.
As a long-term Diablo, Torchlight, Path of Exile and the like player, I figured this would be a solid piece of entertainment to satisfy my needs. As a Viking fan at heart, this looked very promising to me.
However, the game does not even come close to any of these games.
First off, I paid 44.99 EUR for this, which is not cheap.
I was expecting a game worth my money, but it's really not.
The character customization is even worse than Torchlight's (which was cheaper btw).
You get the option between:
- Either male or female preset characters
- 3 different hair colors (Blonde/Black/Ginger)
- A few different hairstyles and jewellery
And that's about it. After that you can pick your class and be on your way. For a price tag this high, I was expecting at least a simple character editor that allows for a few body type changes such as thin/fat, skin color and more hair colors.
The game is polished, sure, but that's about all it seems to be about. It looks nice, but the combat is so unintuitive and boring, that it doesn't animate you to feel excited and amped up.
I've tried a few different combat styles and they are just everything but appealing. Atrocious is what I'd call it.
Lacking so much in so many aspects. The basic attack patterns are the same and I hate the fact that enemies always instantly hit you. Rolling doesn't do anything for small hits, they are just there to dodge the big telegraphed hits.
The different "gifts" (basically special abilities with cooldown) feel unrewarding even when upgraded and I'm doing better just pressing A to kill stuff.
Each mission is repetitive and boring. It's pretty much always: Enter the map, go kill stuff until you reach the boss.
Nothing that interesting, not even the environmental factor adds anything except annoyance.
Multiplayer in this game is the worst, by the way. I got matched at level 4 with a guy who's about to finish the game. You can imagine how "fun" the gameplay was for me after that. And it happens all the time. At level 1 I get a guy telling me he is level 9. And so it continues...
Failed to deliver in every aspect aside from aesthetics. Just because your game looks nice, doesn't mean it feels nice.
It has potential, but this game needs a LOT of work. Not just some tweaks, but a general overhaul. The general idea surely seemed nice, but the approach and execution just failed miserably.
If you expected something to still your hunger for Diablo-esque games, this is not it. It's a waste of money if you ask me.
If this game was priced at like 20 bucks, sure, I'd say buy it. But for 45 bucks? Oh, hell no.
